analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (changelog.d/provider-enabled-filter-wins.md, docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md invariant 10 at head lines 247-252, docs/operations/model-migration.md head lines 77-90). No Swift source or code changes are supplied, so no executable security behavior changed in the evidence.

The docs describe a tightening: with enabled_models set, the provider refuses a coordinator load_model or prefetch_model outside the filter (model_not_selected) and does not converge on desired_models for an unlisted build. Operator-chosen builds therefore stay in place, which narrows coordinator-driven download and load surface on the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider boundary and on provider disk and GPU availability. It does not weaken any threat in the model. It leaves consented Autopilot downloads and placements on their existing gates (invariants 8 and 9).

Operational note: the migration runbook now says that most providers will not converge on a new build until operators run darkbloom switch. This is an availability and rollout effect, not a security regression. It touches T-027 and T-012 only indirectly, because model-hash verification and weight integrity are unchanged. The runbook tells operators to count providers still advertising the previous build before retiring it, which matches the challenge-alibi guidance already in the file.

Unverified contracts: I could not see the implementation (autopilotAllowsModel, operatorFilterAllows, the handlers for load_model and prefetch_model, the switch live-apply path) that the docs claim. The claims that the filter is enforced on every path, that alias-successor promotion only happens inside the filter, and that darkbloom switch applies the filter at once without a restart are unverified. If the code PR is reviewed separately, check that the filter cannot be bypassed via desired_models or Autopilot adoption, and that a live filter update has no race with in-flight loads. No docs-versus-code drift in the threat model is evident. Setting needs_deeper_review because the enforcement code is outside the supplied evidence.
